title: Staged pinning and catalog ingestion for encoder + ranker families
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Goal: provide a repeatable, low-risk flow to onboard encoder + candidate-reranker model pairs into the Redwood model catalog with staged version pinning, per-variant performance profiles, and automated catalog ingestion. This ticket implements the ingestion pipeline and canary pin heuristic so product teams can adopt new encoder or reranker revisions without immediate fleet-wide pinning.

Scope: implement catalog ingestion job that accepts a model bundle manifest (encoder + reranker pair), runs a short smoke evaluation, computes per-workload latency/throughput quantiles, token-cost estimates, and writes a profile artifact. Add a 'staged_pin' lifecycle to the model catalog allowing time-windowed canary pinning (eg. 2% traffic -> 10% -> 100%). Integrate telemetry hooks to the Console for per-pin rollout progress, regression alerts, and rollback triggers.

Out of scope: full offline bench harness for large-scale quantization matrix (separate project). Onboarding UX in Console is a follow-up (PM will file a design ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog ingestion job accepts a signed model bundle manifest and produces a profile.json with latency P50/P95/P99, memory footprint estimate, and token-cost estimate
A staged_pin field is added to the catalog schema and visible via the catalog API
Traffic router supports staged pin percentages and respects canary windows (2%, 10%, 100%) configured per pin rollout
Console telemetry shows rollout percentage and flags any latency/quality regressions as alerts
Automated rollback is triggered when latency P95 exceeds baseline by configurable threshold or reranker quality drop detected on canonical eval set
notes: Initial prototype run on staging showed median ingest time 4m for small bundles (~200MB); memory tuning needed for larger quantized artifacts
Trade-off: we will compute lightweight quality metrics (MRR@10) from a fixed 1k sample eval set during ingestion; heavy offline evals remain external
Routing fallback will prefer older major-version model variants to ensure graceful degradation during canary failures
We will mark staged_pin as opt-in for the first wave of onboardings to limit blast radius
